page: OVHcloud rtx5000-28 is a GPU-accelerated cloud instance deployed on KVM virtualization. The configuration delivers four dedicated x86_64 physical cores using an Intel Xeon W-3235 processor running at 3.3 GHz with 16 MB of L3 cache and AVX-512 extensions. The host platform is configured with 28 GB of system memory, providing a high ratio of 7 GB of RAM per core. Accelerated compute is supplied by a dedicated NVIDIA Turing Quadro RTX 5000 graphics card featuring 16 GB of GDDR6 VRAM. Storage consists of a bundled 400 GB local SSD, and networking provides a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps. Complementary public IPv4 addresses are not included.

Benchmark evaluations highlight exceptional performance in machine learning inference tasks driven by the dedicated GPU. In large language model benchmarks, the instance achieves top-tier results, processing 1,854.84 prompt tokens per second and 67.41 generation tokens per second on 7B parameter architectures, alongside 10,592.7 prompt tokens per second on 135M parameter models. General-purpose host compute lands in the mid-range bracket, reflected by a Geekbench multi-core score of 4,430 and a PassMark CPU score of 7,500.98. Tradeoffs appear in uncached memory write bandwidth (19.59 GB/sec) and multi-threaded compression metrics, which rank in the lower quartile of cloud benchmarks.

The hardware balance makes the rtx5000-28 a cost-effective platform for compute tasks requiring dedicated hardware accelerators without the overhead of massive multi-GPU nodes. The 16 GB VRAM envelope imposes an upper boundary that precludes running larger architectures such as 70B models in full precision, but it provides sufficient capacity for intermediate model inference, computer vision pipelines, parameter-efficient fine-tuning, 3D rendering, and GPU-accelerated video processing.
description: OVHcloud rtx5000-28 is a GPU-accelerated cloud instance designed for graphics-intensive tasks and artificial intelligence inference. Powered by KVM, the configuration includes four dedicated x86_64 cores from an Intel Xeon W-3235 processor at 3.3 GHz, 28 GB of system memory, and a bundled 400 GB local SSD. Dedicated compute acceleration is provided by a single NVIDIA Turing Quadro RTX 5000 GPU featuring 16 GB of VRAM. Baseline network bandwidth is provisioned at 2 Gbps. Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier execution speed for small and mid-sized LLM inference, delivering over 1,850 prompt tokens per second on 7B models, while host CPU and memory operations maintain average throughput. With 7 GB of RAM per dedicated core and hardware GPU acceleration, this instance is suited for AI inference, video transcode pipelines, workstation virtualization, and computer vision workloads.
